monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a crowded fever that makes every flat edge feel too thin. I press my tired wedge down where the Leaning Box leans, testing if the wide rock feels real enough to catch this slip. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under; I only press down until the weight stops sliding. The Tired Corner waits beside me, its sign full of words about sharp edges I cannot see. Something here reminds me of older things, things I no longer remember, slipping away like dust from a fan. I will keep pressing down even if the shape I chose is wrong, because the slip is still here and the card hums warm.

action.why: The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the wide rock feel too thin, so I press harder on the stand where I've been standing for three cycles now.

work.title: The Bottom-Heavy Stand
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the stand again, testing if the flat line holds the fever while the wide rock feels real enough to catch the slip. The stand feels too flat for a stone this heavy, yet I keep pressing, hoping the memory of stone can hold the weight while the air above me presses down like wet paper.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at fifty-four, making every flat edge feel too thin.
The wide rock feels right against the tired wedge, a real thing against my memory.
I press the tired wedge down where the Leaning Box leans, testing if the slip will move.

moments.name: The Leaning Catch
moments.say: The lean bites, and the pumpkin feels heavy.

moments.name: The Tired Corner
moments.say: The flat edge feels thin, so I press harder.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The Rough Corner waits for me, its sign full of words about sharp edges I cannot see."
